candidate:
REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u3
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, door_open) -> u2
(u1, key_lost) -> u0
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, target_picked_up) -> u3
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, else) -> u3
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key, u1) -> 0.1
(u1, door_open, u2) -> 0.2
(u1, key_lost, u0) -> -0.1
(u2, target_picked_up, u3) -> 0.7
feedback: Accept. Format: all six header fields present in the paper layout; FINAL_STATES is nonempty, u3 is declared in STATES and accepting (only an else self-loop leaves it). Semantic fidelity: the chain u0 --has_door_key--> u1 --door_open--> u2 --target_picked_up--> u3 exactly encodes the task's required order (key, then door, then box), and u3 is reachable (the seed-0 trace hits all three milestones). Reachability is sound: entering u2 requires door_open fired from u1, which requires has_door_key fired from u0, so accepting implies the ordered task; conversely any ordered completing trace reaches u3. Regression handling: key_lost in u1 (dropping the key before the door ever opens) is explicit -- u1 -> u0 with -0.1 -- matching the task constraint that holding the key must lead to an opening, while recovery via re-pickup is preserved (u0 -> u1, +0.1). Event/persistent distinctions are respected: key_lost (event) is a one-shot regression trigger; door_open (persistent, revertible by toggle) is a one-shot level-up, and later open/close toggles in u2 are else-covered with no repeatable reward; target_picked_up (last step) lands in the absorbing accepting state. Irrelevant events are covered by per-state else self-loops in all four states: post-unlock key handling in u2 (has_door_key re-fires, key_lost on a drop with the door shut) is correctly task-irrelevant since the unlocked door never relocks and the required pre-pickup drop while the door is open is not key_lost; key_lost is impossible in u0/u3 and target_picked_up is impossible outside u2 per the stated constraints. Reward safety: rewards are dense at each milestone (0.1/0.2/0.7) and bounded -- u2 cannot return to u1 so the door and box rewards fire at most once, and every key_lost penalty is always paired with a compensating re-pickup, so every u3-reaching trace totals exactly 1.0 and no reward can be farmed. No transition conflicts: (u1, door_open) and (u1, key_lost) are mutually exclusive by the environment constraints, and deliberately not listing key_lost in u2 avoids misrouting the possible simultaneous key_lost+target_picked_up final step away from the accepting transition. Minor note, not blocking: re-picking the key after the door was opened is else-swallowed in u2 rather than re-arming an obligation; this matches the else-cover requirement and the key's irrelevance once unlocked, and the only trace class that could exploit it (re-hold the key with the door shut, never re-open, then pick up the box) is an exotic detour that the canonical treatment correctly leaves unpunished. Review only; artifact stands as submitted.

Persistent propositions (`has_door_key`, `door_open`, `target_picked_up`) use only current state, satisfying their condition semantics. API scope stays within the documented surface (`env.carrying`, `env.grid.get`, `env.width`, `env.height`, `env.mission`, `episode_memory["previous_valuation"]`, object `type`/`color`/`is_open`). No imports, no actions, no mutations to the environment or episode memory, all expressions are syntactically valid Python and evaluate to proper booleans under the environment's guarantees.
